subject: Private deployment: licensing, support & $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@optima.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — private/VPC pricing, env count, unit economics

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so everyone is aligned and we can move to a pricing draft: 

Summary of what we heard from Optima AI on the call:
- Typical sustained usage: ~50M tokens / month (inference only); occasional spikes to ~120M tokens for product launches (1–2x per quarter).
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC in us-west region with 3 environments (prod, stage, dev).
- Security: KMS-backed key management required; SOC2 compliance evidence requested.
- Support: leaning toward Premium (24/7 on-call + quarterly architecture reviews).
- Procurement timeline: target contract signed by end of Q3; procurement contact CC'd below.

Commercial asks we need you to confirm so we can finalize the draft: 
1) Expected committed monthly token floor for year-1 (e.g., 30M / 50M / 75M). This affects committed discounts and reserved capacity economics.
2) Preferred licensing model: subscription (annual term + usage) vs term license + annual support.
3) Any target $/1M tokens you want us to hit for internal approval? You mentioned a ballpark during the call — please confirm.

What I'll do next (by Mon EOD):
- Send two pricing scenarios (Subscription + usage and Term license + support) with modeled unit economics for the 50M baseline and 120M spike pattern.
- Include SOW stub for the 3 envs and a checklist for KMS/SOC2 artifacts.
- Loop in Marissa for discount approval if we propose >15% off list.

Attachments: preliminary worksheet (optima-pricing-draft.xlsx) and an SOW template stub (sow-vpc-draft.pdf).

Would you confirm the committed monthly floor and the $/1M token target? If you prefer, drop numbers directly to procurement@optima.ai and I'll take it from there.

Thanks — R

--
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@optima.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Optima AI Procurement <procurement@optima.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — private/VPC pricing, env count

Hi Rachel — thanks for the detailed recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

Committed tokens: we can commit to a 50M tokens/month minimum for Yr1 with the expectation that spikes will bring our avg to ~70–80M across the year. If committing to 12 months we could consider a higher floor (75M) if the unit economics are attractive.

$ target: procurement has a target of ~$100 / 1M tokens (we understand there are other line items for infra/support). If you can show an overall blended $/1M token near that with a 12-month commit, we’ll be in a good spot.

Envs: Confirmed 3 envs (prod, staging, dev). We will need network peering + cross-account IAM setup; KMS is required (we manage keys).

Support: We want Premium (24/7) — willing to pay for it, but need details on response SLAs (P1 < 1 hour) and escalation path. Also want to know if your Premium includes quarterly architecture review and custom tuning sessions.

Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize commercials by 9/30/2026. I’m cc'ing our procurement lead (procurement@optima.ai) for budget/PO cadence.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute slot if helpful.

Best,
Alice
VP Product, Optima AI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@optima.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Optima AI Procurement <procurement@optima.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing scenarios + unit-econ math (draft)

Alice / Procurement team — attaching the updated worksheet and two modeled scenarios. Key points below; full numbers are in optima-pricing-draft.xlsx.

Scenario A — Subscription + usage (recommended for predictable ops)
- Annual subscription (reserved capacity) to cover baseline (50M tokens/mo) + usage for spikes.
- Base subscription: $85k/year (covers reserved capacity and 3 private envs).
- Usage overage: $110 / 1M tokens for on-demand above reserved baseline.
- Premium support add-on: $30k/year (24/7 pager, P1 <1h, quarterly architecture reviews).

Blended math (assumes 50M committed, 120M spike months x2 per quarter averaged into year):
- Annual tokens: ~900M tokens -> effective blended $/1M ≈ $98 (subscription + usage + support amortized).

Scenario B — Term license + annual support (preferred if they want capex/no ongoing usage):
- Term license: $220k (one-time) for the private runtime and perpetual infra license for the model serving software.
- Annual support (premium): $60k/year (includes security reviews, priority engineering time).
- If Optima self-manages infra: remove reserved capacity fee; unit $/1M becomes more dependent on your infra ops.

Blended math for term license (YR1 amortized license + support):
- YR1 effective blended $/1M ≈ $110 (license amortized over 12 months + support + estimated infra).

Discount/commit options
- 12-month commit at 75M/mo baseline: we can price Scenario A with a 12% off list on the subscription line and 10% off overage — requires Marissa approval for >10% total discount.
- We can tighten the blended $/1M to the mid-$90s with an agreed 75M committed floor.

KMS/Security/SOC2
- We support customer-managed KMS in the private deployment and will include SOC2 artifact pack and runbook as part of onboarding.

Next steps I propose:
1) Optima confirms whether 50M floor or 75M is acceptable for a 12-month commit.
2) If they choose Scenario A and commit to 75M, I will request internal approval for a 12% commit discount (Marissa).
3) I’ll share a short commercial term sheet and SOW for legal/procurement review.

Attachments: optima-pricing-draft.xlsx (detailed line items) and sow-vpc-draft.pdf (SOW stub).

If this looks directionally right, Rachel (me) to loop legal and Marissa for discount sign-off.

Thanks — R

--
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
